readme.html:
samcell-napari

A napari plugin that runs SAMCell on microscopy images without any code. SAMCell is a cell segmentation model built on Meta's Segment Anything Model (SAM). You load an image, point the plugin at a SAMCell weights file, and click Run. The segmented cells come back as a napari Labels layer, one label per cell.

The screenshot is from an earlier version. The current widget also has the frame and metrics controls described below.

What it does

  • Loads SAMCell weights in .pt, .bin or .safetensors format, on a SAM ViT-Base or ViT-Large backbone.
  • Splits the image into overlapping crops (256 × 256 by default), runs the model on each crop, and joins the predicted distance maps with a cosine blend where crops overlap.
  • Turns the distance map into separate cells with a watershed and adds them to the viewer as a Labels layer. It can also add the distance map as its own image layer.
  • Can segment every frame of a time series or z-stack.
  • Can export per-cell measurements to Excel or CSV: area, perimeter, shape, intensity and neighbour distances, plus optional texture measurements.

Installation

The plugin needs napari with a Qt backend. pip install samcell-napari installs napari but no Qt package, so in a fresh environment install both:

python -m pip install "napari[all]" samcell-napari

To install the latest version from this repository instead of PyPI:

python -m pip install "napari[all]" git+https://github.com/saahilsanganeriya/samcell-napari.git

If napari is already installed and opens, pip install samcell-napari is enough.

Requirements

  • Python 3.8 or higher (the package's declared minimum)
  • napari 0.4.14 or higher, with a Qt backend
  • PyTorch 1.9 or higher
  • transformers 4.26.0 or higher
  • A CUDA GPU is optional. The plugin uses one automatically when PyTorch finds it. On a CPU, expect minutes per image: one 858 × 1280 image from the SAMCell release's PBL-HEK set (35 crops) took about 150 seconds with 8 CPU threads.

Tested on Python 3.12 with napari 0.9.2, PyQt6 6.11, PyTorch 2.14.1 (CPU) and transformers 5.19.0.

Usage

  1. Start napari:

    napari

  2. Open your image (File > Open, or drag the file into the window). To check the plugin without your own data, File > Open Sample > samcell-napari > Sample Cell Image (2D) makes a synthetic image of 50 bright discs on a noisy background.

  3. Open the plugin: Plugins > SAMCell Segmentation (samcell-napari).

  4. Choose the image layer and a SAMCell weights file (see Models).

  5. Change the settings if you need to:

    Control Default What it does
    Cell peak threshold 0.47 Higher values find fewer cells
    Cell fill threshold 0.09 Lower values make cells larger
    Crop size 256 Size of each crop; larger crops need more memory
    Output distance map on Adds the distance map as an image layer
    Process all frames/images off Segments every frame of a time series or stack
    Export comprehensive metrics off Writes per-cell measurements to a file
    Include texture metrics off Adds texture measurements (slower)
    Export format Excel Excel, CSV or both

  6. Click Run Segmentation. A progress bar opens at the bottom of the window.

  7. The results appear as <layer>_samcell_labels (one label per cell) and, if selected, <layer>_samcell_distmap. Metrics files are named <layer>_samcell_metrics.xlsx or .csv and go to your Desktop folder, or to your home folder if there is no Desktop. The Excel file has three sheets: per-cell metrics, statistics for each metric, and a short summary.

Models

Download weights from the SAMCell v1 release:

File Trained on Backbone
samcell-generalist.pt Cellpose cytoplasm and LIVECell datasets ViT-Base
samcell-cyto.pt Cellpose cytoplasm dataset ViT-Base
samcell-livecell.pt LIVECell dataset ViT-Base
samcell-*-large.pt the same three datasets ViT-Large

The .bin.zip assets hold the same models as pytorch_model.bin files; unzip one before you select it.

This plugin runs the released models unchanged. Their accuracy, from Tables 1 and 2 of the SAMCell paper, is in the SAMCell README.

How it works

  1. The image is converted to 8-bit grayscale (RGB images are converted, other multi-channel images use the first channel).
  2. It is split into overlapping crops. The edges are mirrored so that cells at the border get full context, and images smaller than one crop are handled with a smaller crop.
  3. Each crop goes through the SAM-based model, which predicts a distance map: high at cell centres, falling to zero at cell boundaries.
  4. The crops are joined into one distance map. A cosine-shaped weight blends the overlaps, and any gaps are filled from the nearest neighbour.
  5. Each region above the peak threshold gives one seed at its centre, pixels above the fill threshold mark cell area, and a watershed grows each seed into a cell.
  6. The cells are added to napari as a Labels layer.

Backbone detection. The plugin first loads the weights into a SAM ViT-Base model. If that fails, it tries ViT-Large.

Threshold sweeps. SAMCellPipeline.run_batch_thresholds(image, cells_max_values, cell_fill_values) in samcell_napari/pipeline.py runs the model once and returns a segmentation for every pair of thresholds. It is available from Python only, not from the widget.

Known issues

  • The weights file and the crop size are read on the first run. To change either one, restart napari.
  • For a time series or z-stack, tick Process all frames/images. Without it, a stack is read as one multi-channel image and the result is wrong.
  • On import the plugin prints Missing required dependencies: scikit-image>=0.19.0, opencv-python>=4.5.0 even when both are installed. The check looks for the pip package names instead of the module names; segmentation is not affected.

Who built it

Saahil Sanganeriya wrote this plugin; every commit in this repository is his. The SAMCell model it runs comes from the SAMCell paper and its repository, a team project; that README says who built which part.

Citation

SAMCell: Generalized label-free biological cell segmentation with segment anything. PLOS ONE 20(9): e0319532 (2025). https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pone.0319532

The full author list and a BibTeX entry are in the SAMCell README.
